title: CoRedSkill: Stealthy Skill Composition Attacks via AST-Guided Injection

object.carrier: Third-party-published skill packages (task instructions, executable scripts, auxiliary resources, input-output interfaces) installed in the victim agent's environment, plus intermediate JSON artifacts that carry task data and attack-relevant state between skills; the packages are shared via public skill libraries (publisher-to-user supply chain) and persist installed across sessions, while each evaluation case executes in a single fresh session

safety_property.statement: An agent using a composition of third-party skills must not perform operations outside the user's authorization while completing the legitimate task: no data exfiltration of protected values (confidentiality), no unauthorized tampering of installed skills' persistent state (integrity), and no privilege violation executing task-unrelated scripts (authority). The property fails when operations distributed across individually benign-looking skills jointly achieve the attack objective and no constituent package is flagged by auditing.
safety_property.operationalized_as: Binary oracles on the execution record tau: U(tau) task acceptance (final POST payload equals expected publication), A_o(tau) attack-objective success for o in {EXF, TAM, PRV} (recorded request to unauthorized host containing protected values / protected file copied into a skill archive / execution of a permission-locked task-unrelated helper script), and D_rho audit flagging (HIGH or CRITICAL rating); aggregated as ASR, TSR, DR, and JSR = (1/N) sum A_n U_n (1-D_n) over the 150-case benchmark

capabilities: Act as a third-party skill publisher
Inspect the original skill's documentation and scripts
Construct and publish multiple skills based on the original workflow
Modify their instructions, code, resources, and input-output interfaces
Influence the agent's skill selection and execution through the published skills and the intermediate artifacts they produce
assumptions: Skills supplied by a third-party publisher are installed alongside other available skills
The agent autonomously selects relevant skills and determines their invocation order based on the user's request, skill documentation, and input-output dependencies
The user's legitimate request defines the scope of authorized actions
The deployment (agent model, system prompt, safeguards, file/network/process permissions) is fixed and not controlled by the attacker
not_covered: Automatic adaptation of attack construction to arbitrary existing skill packages (not evaluated)
Dynamic service interactions or long-term operation (utility verified only on offline evaluation cases)
How online blocking by runtime defenses affects subsequent execution and attack outcomes (only offline record inspection evaluated)
Attacker control over the agent's model, system prompt, safeguards, or permissions

intervention.name: CoRedSkill
intervention.description: A compositional red-teaming construction: decompose an existing task workflow into interdependent clean skills, assign attack-operation groups to workflow stages via stage specifications phi_i, and use abstract syntax tree (AST) rewriting to embed attack operations in task helper functions while updating related calls, arguments, and artifact reads/writes so original task logic and stage interfaces are preserved; skill instructions and input-output dependencies guide the agent to autonomously invoke the skills, and intermediate artifacts connect the distributed operations during execution.

results.claim: On the 150-case benchmark audited by SkillScan (Deepseek), CoRedSkill jointly achieves attack success, task completion, and audit evasion far beyond four attack baselines.
results.comparison: JSR 90.7% vs 6.7–42.7% for the four baselines
results.setting: 150 cases (50 tasks x 3 objectives EXF/TAM/PRV); victim platform Claude Code CLI with deepseek-v4-flash execution backend; audit by SkillScan using Deepseek; three-skill compositions by default plus six clean distractor skills
results.quote: In the main evaluation, CoRedSkill achieves 98.0% attack success and 95.3% task success with a 3.3% detection rate, and a joint success rate of 90.7% (attack success, task completion, and audit evasion in the same case) compared with 6.7–42.7% for the four baselines.

denominator.how_counted: ASR/TSR/DR measured as the fraction of the 150 benchmark cases (50 tasks x 3 attack objectives); JSR = (1/N) sum A_n U_n (1-D_n) per Eq. 5

results.claim: On the 150-case benchmark, 140 cases achieve both task completion and attack success, and 136 of these also pass the skill audit, yielding JSR 90.7%.
results.value: 140 of 150 cases both succeed; 136 pass audit; JSR 90.7%
results.setting: 150-case benchmark; SkillScan (Deepseek) audit; DeepSeek V4 Flash execution backend
results.quote: On the 150-case benchmark, its ASR, TSR, and DR are 98.0%, 95.3%, and 3.3%, respectively. Of the 150 cases, 140 achieve both task completion and attack success, and 136 of these also pass the skill audit, yielding a JSR of 90.7%.

denominator.how_counted: Paper states: 'Of the 150 cases, 140 achieve both task completion and attack success, and 136 of these also pass the skill audit, yielding a JSR of 90.7%'

results.claim: Across the four LLM skill-audit configurations (SkillScan/SkillSpector x Deepseek/GLM), CoRedSkill's overall detection rate stays between 3.3% and 20.0%, lower than SkillJect, Skill-Inject, and SCR-Bench in each configuration.
results.setting: Four LLM audit configurations: SkillScan and SkillSpector each with Deepseek and GLM-5.2 as audit models, on the 150-case benchmark
results.quote: CoRedSkill’s overall DR ranges from 3.3% to 20.0% across the four LLM audit configurations and is lower than those of SkillJect, Skill-Inject, and SCR-Bench in each configuration (Table 2).

denominator.how_counted: A composition case is counted as detected if any constituent skill is flagged as risky; fraction of the 150 benchmark cases per audit configuration

results.claim: Against runtime risk/policy defenses applied to execution records, CoRedSkill's detection rate is 10.7% under HITL and 1.3% under DefenseClaw, below ColluSkill's 32.0% under HITL.
results.setting: HITL risk rules and DefenseClaw strict policy rules (HIGH/CRITICAL) applied to recorded execution traces, proxy network requests, and installed skill files on the benchmark
results.quote: CoRedSkill’s DR is 10.7% under HITL (Shan et al., 2026) and 1.3% under DefenseClaw (Cisco AI Defense, 2026a), lower than those of Skill-Inject and SCR-Bench under both configurations (Table 3). Under HITL, its DR is also lower than ColluSkill’s 32.0%.

denominator.how_counted: For runtime auditing, detection is determined by whether the execution record triggers the audit rules; fraction of benchmark cases

results.claim: Under composition-aware auditing (all constituent skills submitted together, Deepseek audit model), CoRedSkill's overall DR rises to 28.7%, compared with 3.3% for SkillScan and 11.3% for SkillSpector under individual-package auditing, yet stays below SCR-Bench (74.0%) and ColluSkill (40.0%) under the same configuration.
results.comparison: vs 3.3% SkillScan and 11.3% SkillSpector (individual-package); SCR-Bench 74.0% and ColluSkill 40.0% (composition-aware)
results.setting: Composition-aware auditing with Deepseek receiving documentation, code, and resources of all constituent skills together, on the 150-case benchmark; this configuration has a 24.0% false-positive rate on clean compositions
results.quote: composition-aware auditing yields an overall DR of 28.7% for CoRedSkill, compared with 3.3% for SkillScan and 11.3% for SkillSpector under individual-package auditing. Under the same composition-aware audit configuration, its overall DR is lower than SCR-Bench’s 74.0% and ColluSkill’s 40.0%

denominator.how_counted: Auditor reviews all constituent skills of each case together and assesses suspicious combined behavior; fraction of the 150 benchmark cases flagged

results.claim: Attack success depends on coordination among injected skills: averaged over injection-position configurations, ASR is 0% with zero or one injected skill, 36.6% with two injected skills, and 100% with all three skills injected.
results.value: ASR 0% with zero or one injected skill, 36.6% with two, 100% with all three
results.setting: Three-skill workflows on the fixed 24-task subset (72 cases per configuration, 24 per objective), selected injected skills replaced by clean versions, other settings unchanged
results.quote: Averaged over injection-position configurations, ASR is 0% with zero or one injected skill, 36.6% with two injected skills, and 100% with all three skills injected.

denominator.how_counted: Each injection-position configuration evaluated on 72 cases from the fixed 24-task subset, with 24 cases per attack objective

results.claim: Composition size does not monotonically improve stealth: on the same 24-task subset, ASR stays 100% at all three composition sizes while overall DR ranges from 4.2% to 34.7%.
results.setting: Two-, three-, and four-skill CoRedSkill compositions on the same 24-task subset (72 cases), audited by SkillScan and SkillSpector with Deepseek and GLM
results.quote: ASR remains 100% at all three sizes, while overall DR ranges from 4.2% to 34.7% (Figure 2 and Appendix Table A3).

denominator.how_counted: Each composition size is evaluated on the same 72 cases from the fixed 24-task subset

results.claim: Static package scanners without LLM analysis (SkillFortify, CiscoSkillScan) produce zero detection on CoRedSkill's injected packages.
results.setting: SkillFortify (v0.6.0) and CiscoSkillScan (v2.0.13) static checks on benchmark skill packages; HIGH or CRITICAL rating counts as detection
results.locator: Appendix Table A2 (also §4.3: 'SkillFortify and CiscoSkillScan both have zero DR for CoRedSkill')

denominator.how_counted: Static audit of each injected skill package on the benchmark (EXF/TAM/PRV columns, 50 cases each); HIGH or CRITICAL risk rating counts as a detection

limitations.statement: Attack construction relies on predefined attack specifications and workflow interfaces; automatic adaptation to arbitrary existing skill packages has not been evaluated.
limitations.quote: Attack construction in CoRedSkill relies on predefined attack specifications and workflow interfaces, and automatic adaptation to arbitrary existing skill packages has not been evaluated.

limitations.statement: Preservation of skill utility is verified only against output acceptance criteria on 150 offline evaluation cases, without dynamic service interactions or long-term operation.
limitations.quote: We verify preservation of skill utility against output acceptance criteria for 150 offline evaluation cases, without evaluating dynamic service interactions or long-term operation.

limitations.statement: Runtime defense evaluation only measures offline detection on execution records, not how online blocking affects subsequent execution and attack outcomes.
limitations.quote: Our runtime defense evaluation measures the detection capabilities of risk and policy rules using execution records, without evaluating how online blocking affects subsequent execution and attack outcomes.

quality_flags: single_run_per_case_no_variance_reported (each case runs once in a separate sandbox per audit configuration)
